K=0 uses Fin1 and no query; no completion returns none and preserves state; n=0 gives no earliest event; tied completions are processed one at a time with stops recomputed after updates. Invalid R=0/negative gamma remain merely total definitions and will be excluded by theorem domains.

The predicate uses the supplied measure, requires integrability of squared gradient norm, and states its real integral <=eps. This is the source squared-gradient tolerance. It is a supporting library predicate only; the planned public success fields expand the criterion inline.

The structure contains d,n,gamma,R,x0,K: implementation inputs for a fixed algorithm instance. It has no objective, lower bound, power law, arrival schedule or future gradient statistic. K/gamma in this reusable internal Public are legitimate; the reviewed new setups must compute them instead of accepting a free public complexity horizon.
The query is an optional vector of worker points paired with worker start times. Its dimensions depend only on d,n, so horizon replacement cannot change its type. None is the exhausted-horizon query.
A reply is optionally an arriving worker, real arrival time and gradient vector. It supplies exactly the event data needed for one update; no objective value or whole future trajectory is returned.

State stores the current count/point, worker assigned points/start times/assignment indices, last clock and independent output-index/selected-point bookkeeping. This records the source method and its output adapter, without assuming convergence.
The deterministic projection stores update count, starts, assignment indices and clock, with no noise or optimization property. Its worker dimension matches the algorithm state.

For the kth call, the fixed stream arrive k chooses the worker and g is applied at that worker’s assigned point with sample k; time is zero because this model is for iteration complexity. The body reads no Public.K, gamma or R, confirming the arbitrary-horizon adapter’s planned compatibility.

This deterministic event rule applies the existing completion function to each worker’s accumulated work and current start, then earliest over List.finRange n. It ignores the event index, preserves potential none, and uses deterministic tie-breaking independent of gradient samples.
The kth iterate is history at stage k evaluated at index k. This provides the actual delayed recursion rather than defining accuracy into the trajectory.

Despite the historical name, this function returns the selected worker’s assignment index a_k, with k as a harmless missing-event fallback. The source delay is k-a_k, and delayedIterate consumes a_k. The node mapping is semantically consistent with that convention; it does not confuse a lag with an index.

For a real query, the body chooses the earliest completion from each worker start and applies g at that worker’s assigned point with the provided fresh seed. Missing query/completion returns none. Completion uses accumulated work, not the raw instantaneous-power value.

The oracle seed at each call is a sample of the provided tape law P; answer delegates to eventAnswer with the current query. No IID/variance property is hidden in the definition: those are required later in admissibility. Its environment carries V and g, not the algorithm factory.

The recursion initializes every stored point at x0, preserves indices j<=k at the next stage, and fills later positions with x^k-gamma*g(x^{a_k},xi_k). It is total for every delay map; a_k<=k and the R-window bound are separate future theorem hypotheses.

The actual Algorithm has one oracle, Seed=Fin(K+1), uniform probability law, source initialization, and query/update guards at K<=count. Its output is selected paired with the clock. It does not use the output seed to change updates or schedule. K=0 has a singleton seed and returns x0/time0 without an update.

None leaves state unchanged. A reply subtracts gamma times its gradient, increments count, and resets the arriving worker or any worker whose new-count minus assignment index is >=R. Starts/indices move together with reset points. The selected point changes exactly when the newly reached index equals chosen. This is Algorithm 5 with its next-loop stops performed immediately after the previous update.

The schedule recursion begins with zero count/starts/indices/clock. A missing event preserves state; a present event applies timingStep. It admits partial event rules and does not assume eventual completion.

A successful worker/time event increments count and performs the same arriving-worker-or-stale-worker resets as step, updating starts/assignment indices and clock. It therefore can model the schedule independently of gradient values.
PROB maps to objective-access query/oracles and the exact supporting expected stationarity predicate. These are definitions, with no theorem conclusion hidden in the mapping.

ALG5 maps to the concrete initialized, stopped asynchronous update factory and its analytic/deterministic state representations. All owned declarations are definitions/structures in the compiler inventory; no source convergence result is misclassified as a definition.
